scenario: AITA for telling my mother she is the reason I won't wear white to my wedding? | I'm engaged. Planning on a small semi-formal beach wedding. Mum tells me that she can't wait to go wedding dress shopping with me and she wants to book an appointment at this fancy bridal shop in town. I told mum that I didn't want a white dress and that shop did just white bridal dresses and nothing else (I'd already looked it up). I think the whole concept of white wedding dresses is stupid. It only started with Queen Vic so it's not some ancient tradition and the ship has sailed on the whole white = pure/innocent/virginal thing. However, the main and the defining reason I am anti white wedding dress, is that my mother wore a white dress when she got married, and she and dad are divorced now. Every other woman in my family has worn a coloured dress to get married in (usually either blue or red and either really pale or really dark, with not much in between) and they have all had long (mostly) happy marriages that were either til death did them part or are still going strong today. When mum asked why I didn't want a white dress I first gave the the Queen Vic line which mum said wasn't enough justification, and then the bit about how I'm not exactly "innocent", which was an awful conversation to have with my mother. When she said that wasn't good enough I said "because I just don't want a white dress and I think coloured dresses look nicer and it's my wedding so I get to pick my clothes". Mum asked a few more times what the real reason was and I eventually admitted that her being the only woman to break the tradition and also the only woman to get divorced didn't exactly instill me with confidence in white dresses. Mum got really quiet, then I saw she was crying. She said she tried her best and that I spoke to her like that when I know how the divorce upset her was really cruel. I haven't apologised yet but I feel like she backed me into a corner and wouldn't accept any of the 3 perfectly fine answers I'd given before that, and I shouldn't have had to justify myself to begin with as it is my wedding so the only people whose opinions matter are me and my fiance. I also feel like if she had just accepted my choice or any of the first 3 answers I gave then I would not be in this situation. AITA?

But here's the thing: I don't want a white dress, and that shop only does white bridal dresses. I already looked it up, so I know that's their specialty. I think the whole white wedding dress thing is kind of silly. It started with Queen Victoria, so it's not some ancient tradition. Plus, the idea that white symbolizes purity, innocence, or virginity is outdated and doesn't resonate with me. I mean, I'm not exactly "innocent," and I don't think that's the right way to define myself on my wedding day. But the main reason I'm against a white dress is personal. My mom wore a white dress when she got married, and she and my dad are now divorced. Every other woman in my family has worn a colored dressâĢĶusually blue or red, either really pale or really dark. And guess what? They've all had long, mostly happy marriages, some even until death did them part. So, seeing that pattern, I feel like colored dresses might bring better luck or at least align more with my family's experiences. When my mom asked why I didn't want a white dress, I first mentioned the Queen Victoria thing, but she didn't think that was enough justification. Then I brought up the part about not being "innocent," which was an awful conversation to have with my mom. She said that wasn't good enough, so I finally admitted that her being the only one to break the tradition and also the only one to get divorced didn't exactly make me confident in white dresses. My mom got really quiet, and I saw she was crying. She said she tried her best and that I spoke to her like that when I know how the divorce upset her was really cruel. I haven't apologized yet, but I feel like she backed me into a corner and wouldn't accept any of the first three perfectly fine answers I gave before that. I shouldn't have had to justify myself to begin with because it's my wedding, and the only people whose opinions matter are me and my fiancÃ©. I also feel like if she had just accepted my choice or any of the first three answers I gave, then I wouldn't be in this situation. So, is it AITA (Ask If Tolerable, Assume Not) for me to tell my mom that she's the reason I won't wear white to my wedding? Alright, so to figure this out, I need to consider a few things: 1. **Communication Styles**: How did I communicate my reasons? Was it respectful, or did it come off as blaming or hurtful? 2. **Family Dynamics**: How does this situation fit into our family's history, especially regarding past conflicts or sensitive topics like divorce? 3. **Personal Boundaries**: Is it reasonable for me to assert my preferences for my own wedding, or should I be more accommodating of my mom's wishes? 4. **Emotional Impact**: How did my mom react, and what does that tell me about the impact of my words? 5. **Cultural and Personal Significance**: Why do I feel so strongly about the color of my dress? Is it tied to personal experiences, cultural traditions, or something else? 6. **Resolution Possibilities**: How can I mend this situation?
